questions.prompt: When should the shell check read echo text and heredoc text as data instead of as possible write targets? Option 1: only when every program in the whole command is on a short list of programs that run no text (cd, pushd, popd, echo, printf, cat, tee, ls, pwd, mkdir, true, and git add/commit/push/status/diff/log/show). Option 2: the brief's wording, where heredoc text needs a safe reader (cat, tee, git commit -F -), echo text must not be piped, and no interpreter, eval, source, '.', exec or xargs may appear anywhere in the command.

options.label: Closed list of programs that run no text (Recommended)
options.description: Text is data only when every program in the command is on the list; anything else keeps today's reading. Plan file, section 'The grammar reduceDataText accepts', paragraph 'Program allow-list', and Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity, item 2.
options.pros: Also closes the routes a list of interpreter names misses: a script just written and run as ./s, a function or alias named cat or echo, PATH=. cat, and git -c alias. A mistake in the new reader can only matter for commands built from programs that run nothing.
options.cons: A command that mixes an echo or heredoc naming a protected file with any other program (npm test, node, rm) is still refused, as it is today; such a command has to be split into two calls.

options.label: Safe reader for heredocs plus a list of interpreter names
options.description: As the brief words it: heredoc text needs cat, tee or git commit -F - as its reader, echo text must not be piped, and the command must not name bash, sh, zsh, node, python and the rest, or eval, source, '.', exec or xargs.
options.pros: Fewer commands keep today's reading, so fewer false refusals remain. The safe-reader and no-pipe rules already go further than the first attempt, which was taken out after nine bypasses.
options.cons: Programs that run text without an interpreter's name still get through unless each one is found and added: ./s after a heredoc wrote s, a redefined cat, PATH=. cat, git -c alias.
